tasks.title: Lane rail hover on the swimlane, the Matriarch's hover surface, and the dot's flex (C6, C7, C8)
acceptance: C67-resolver. The assertions below are evaluated by resolving, for a stated row state, which `background` declaration in `LaneRail.module.css` wins: by selector specificity, then by source order. jsdom computes no CSS-module cascade (`LaneRail.styles.test.ts` docblock), so the cascade has to be resolved from the sheet's text. Whatever does the resolving carries positive controls on inline fixture sheets, each with its predicted winner stated in the test. They are: (1) of two equal-specificity rules, the later one wins; (2) a higher-specificity earlier rule beats a lower-specificity later one; (3) a `:hover` rule does not apply to an unhovered state; (4) a near-miss selector, `.rowMain:hover`, is not treated as matching the `.row` element. This encodes the session decision that every new stylesheet scanner carries both a must-match fixture and a near-miss fixture. Evidence: `npm test -- src/renderer/src/lanes/LaneRail.styles.test.ts` passes.

C7-inner. No hover background is painted on the inner button. `LaneRail.module.css` has no `.rowMain:hover` rule, and no rule whose selector contains both `.rowMain` and `:hover` declares `background`. Base has one, at lines 163-165. This encodes the `.row` docblock at base lines 77-88: the `<li>` swimlane, not `.rowMain`, is where a row-wide background belongs. Evidence: a test in `LaneRail.styles.test.ts`, run by the same command.

C7-calf. An unselected Calf row, hovered, resolves its `.row` background to `var(--oc-bg-hover)`. At base it resolves to no `.row` background. Evidence: the C67-resolver test command. Discrimination: delete the new row-hover rule, observe the failure, revert.

C7-matriarch. An unselected Matriarch row (`data-matriarch='true'`), hovered, resolves to `var(--oc-bg-hover)`. At base it resolves to `var(--oc-bg-raised)`, from base line 100. Evidence: the same command. Discrimination: delete or reorder the rule that paints the hovered unselected Matriarch so that `.row[data-matriarch='true']` wins, observe the failure, revert.

C7-selected-primary (deliberately preserved behaviour). A primary-pane Calf (`data-in-primary-pane='true'`), hovered, still resolves to `var(--oc-bg-selected)`. A selected row keeps reading as selected while hovered, following the PodBar precedent `.tabItemActive:hover` at `PodBar.module.css:69-71`. Evidence: the same command. Discrimination: delete the rule that keeps a hovered selected row selected, observe the failure, revert.

C7-selected-follower (deliberately preserved behaviour). A follower-pane Calf (`data-in-follower-pane='true'`), hovered, still resolves to `var(--oc-bg-selected)`. Evidence and discrimination: the same as C7-selected-primary.

C6-primary. A primary-pane Matriarch, hovered, resolves to `var(--oc-bg-selected)`. That is a surface distinct from both its selected `--oc-bg-hover` and its unselected `--oc-bg-raised`. At base it resolves to `var(--oc-bg-hover)`, from base line 138, so hover feedback vanishes. Evidence: the same command. Discrimination: delete the Matriarch selected-hover rule, observe the failure, revert.

C6-follower. A follower-pane Matriarch, hovered, resolves to `var(--oc-bg-selected)`. At base it resolves to `var(--oc-bg-hover)`, from base line 142. Evidence and discrimination: the same as C6-primary.

C67-background-only. Every rule whose selector targets `.row` with `:hover` declares `background` and no other property. Hovering therefore cannot overpaint the follower edge or the focused-follower ring (`box-shadow`, base lines 126 and 146). This follows `PodBar.module.css:59-60` ('It sets `background` only… so it cannot sit on top of a focused control's focus ring') and encodes the frontend discipline rule 'Focus is visible'. Evidence: a test in `LaneRail.styles.test.ts`.

C6-comment. The comment above the selected-Matriarch rules (base `LaneRail.module.css:129-136`) no longer says the Matriarch 'darkens rather than brightening on selection': by `styles/tokens.css:27-28` its move from `--oc-bg-raised` (#22262e) to `--oc-bg-hover` (#2b303a) brightens. The comment states the move correctly and also names the hovered selected Matriarch's surface from C6. Evidence: `grep -c "darkens rather than brightening" src/renderer/src/lanes/LaneRail.module.css` prints 0 (base prints 1), and read the comment. Added at Gate 2.

C8. The `.dot` rule in `LaneRail.module.css` declares `flex: none`, matching `.statusDot` at `PodBar.module.css:120-123`. Base `.dot` (lines 216-221) has no `flex`. Evidence: a test asserting `block('.dot')` matches `/flex:\s*none/`, in `LaneRail.styles.test.ts`. Shown able to fail: run it against the rule without the declaration.

T4-preserved (deliberately preserved behaviour). The existing assertions in the describes '(criterion 3)', '(criterion 4)' and '(criterion 5)' of `LaneRail.styles.test.ts` (opening at base lines 101, 141 and 184) are neither removed nor weakened. That includes the three distinct unhovered surfaces at :144-154, where the selected Matriarch is `--oc-bg-hover`. They all pass, and the sheet still hardcodes no colour. Evidence: `npm test -- src/renderer/src/lanes` exits 0.

tasks.title: useDialogFocus moved to shell/ and adopted by both Pod dialogs (C11)
acceptance: C11-move. `src/renderer/src/shell/use-dialog-focus.ts` exists and exports `useDialogFocus`. `src/renderer/src/beachcomber/use-dialog-focus.ts` no longer exists. Every importer OUTSIDE `src/renderer/src/shell/` imports the hook from `../shell/use-dialog-focus`, the relative form other `shell/` imports already use (for example `../shell/contract-runtime`); a file inside `shell/` (such as `shell/use-dialog-focus.test.tsx`) imports it as `./use-dialog-focus`. Evidence: `grep -rn "use-dialog-focus'" src` lists only `../shell/use-dialog-focus` specifiers from files outside `shell/` and only `./use-dialog-focus` specifiers from files inside it, and no specifier names `beachcomber/use-dialog-focus`. The hook's docblock no longer describes it as Beachcomber's alone.

C11-always-mounted. The hook captures the opener when the dialog OPENS, not when its component mounts, and restores when the dialog CLOSES, not only on unmount. Both Pod dialogs are always mounted (`PodsChrome.tsx:219,228` at base) and return null while closed, so the hook as it stands at base (`useEffect` with mount/unmount capture and restore, base lines 54-66) cannot serve them. Evidence: C11-D-restore and C11-N-restore below, each of which mounts the dialog closed before the opener is focused.

C11-beachcomber (deliberately preserved behaviour). Beachcomber's focus behaviour is unchanged. Evidence: `npm test -- src/renderer/src/beachcomber/BeachcomberPreviewDialog.test.tsx` passes, with that file not modified by T5 (T5 does not own it). That includes 'has an accessible name and receives focus when it opens', the trap test, 'returns focus to the control that opened it' and 'puts focus somewhere visible when the opener is gone by the time it closes' (base :178-260).

C11-D-open (deliberately preserved behaviour). When `DeletePodDialog` opens, focus is on the dialog element (`DELETE_POD_TEST_IDS.dialog`), as base `DeletePodDialog.tsx:89-93` does. Base has no test of this. Evidence: a new test in `DeletePodDialog.test.tsx`, run by `npm test -- src/renderer/src/pods`. Discrimination: remove the open-focus call, observe the failure, revert.

C11-D-trap-forward. In `DeletePodDialog`, Tab from the last focusable control (Delete) moves focus to the first focusable control inside the dialog. Evidence: a test in `DeletePodDialog.test.tsx` using `userEvent` `tab()`. The test renders a focusable control OUTSIDE the dialog (after it in document order) and asserts focus never lands on it, because `userEvent.tab()` wraps around the document and, with the dialog rendered alone, would wrap to the dialog's first control at base and pass vacuously. With that outside control present it fails at base, where focus leaves the dialog. Encodes the frontend discipline rule 'Focus … moves predictably after an action that changes what is on screen'.

C11-D-trap-backward. In `DeletePodDialog`, Shift+Tab from the first focusable control, or from the dialog element itself, moves focus to the last focusable control. Evidence: a test in `DeletePodDialog.test.tsx` that renders a focusable control OUTSIDE the dialog (before it in document order) and asserts focus never lands on it. With that outside control present it fails at base.

C11-D-restore. In `DeletePodDialog.test.tsx`, a test does the following: render the dialog CLOSED (`pod={null}`) beside an opener button, focus the opener, rerender with a Pod, then rerender with `pod={null}`. It asserts that `document.activeElement` is the opener. Evidence: `npm test -- src/renderer/src/pods`. It fails at base, where focus is lost to `<body>`. Discrimination: inject a mount-time capture (the base hook's shape), observe the failure, revert.

C11-D-fallback. In `DeletePodDialog.test.tsx`, a test does the following: open the dialog from an opener, remove that opener (unmount it, as a successful delete removes the tab's delete control), then close. It asserts that focus is on the fallback element passed to the dialog, and not on `<body>`. Evidence: the same command. It fails at base.

C11-D-wired. Driven through the real `App` in `pod-lifecycle.test.tsx`: after a delete that succeeds, the dialog closes and the Pod's tab is gone, and `document.activeElement` is the outermost element `PodsChrome` renders. That element is made programmatically focusable with `tabIndex={-1}`, the precedent `BeachcomberPanel.tsx:40-41,78` follows for its `fallbackFocusRef`. Focus is not on `<body>`. Evidence: `npm test -- src/renderer/src/pods/pod-lifecycle.test.tsx`. It fails at base.

C11-N-open (deliberately preserved behaviour). When `NewPodDialog` opens, focus is on the title field (`TEST_IDS.newPodTitleInput`). Evidence: the existing test 'focuses the title field when it opens' (base `NewPodDialog.test.tsx:216-219`) passes unweakened. If the hook gains an initial-focus option to serve this, Beachcomber does not pass it and keeps focusing its dialog element (C11-beachcomber).

C11-N-trap-forward. In `NewPodDialog`, Tab from the last enabled focusable control moves focus to the first (the title field). Evidence: a test in `NewPodDialog.test.tsx` that renders a focusable control OUTSIDE the dialog (after it in document order) and asserts focus never lands on it, so `userEvent.tab()`'s document wrap cannot make it pass vacuously. With that outside control present it fails at base.

C11-N-trap-backward. In `NewPodDialog`, Shift+Tab from the title field moves focus to the last enabled focusable control. Evidence: a test in `NewPodDialog.test.tsx` that renders a focusable control OUTSIDE the dialog (before it in document order) and asserts focus never lands on it. With that outside control present it fails at base.

C11-N-restore. In `NewPodDialog.test.tsx`, a test does the following: render with `open={false}` beside an opener, focus the opener, rerender with `open={true}`, then with `open={false}`. It asserts that focus is on the opener. Evidence: `npm test -- src/renderer/src/pods`. It fails at base. Discrimination: the same mount-time-capture injection as C11-D-restore.

C11-N-fallback. In `NewPodDialog.test.tsx`: the opener is removed before the dialog closes, and focus lands on the fallback element passed to the dialog, not on `<body>`. Evidence: the same command. It fails at base.

C11-N-wired. Driven through the real `App` in `pod-lifecycle.test.tsx`: open New Pod from the empty-workspace control (`EmptyWorkspace`, which unmounts once a Pod is active), then create a Pod. `document.activeElement` is then PodsChrome's outermost element, not `<body>`. Evidence: `npm test -- src/renderer/src/pods/pod-lifecycle.test.tsx`. It fails at base.

C11-props. The fallback reaches each Pod dialog as an internal prop. For New Pod it goes on `NewPodDialogInternalProps`, the existing extension at `NewPodDialog.tsx:29`, and `NewPodDialogProps` in `src/renderer/src/contracts/renderer-view.ts` is not modified (T5 does not own it).

T5-typecheck. `npm run typecheck` exits 0. The move changes an import surface. T5 runs after every task that injects defects into production files (T1-T4), so no peer's injection is live during this repo-wide command.
T5-scope. `npm test -- src/renderer/src/pods src/renderer/src/beachcomber src/renderer/src/shell` exits 0.

tasks.title: Test-guard narrowing and relaxing (C9, U1, U2)
acceptance: C9-bars. The test 'takes elapsedMs pre-computed off the view model and only formats it' in `LaneRow.source.test.ts` applies one named predicate that flags exactly the React hooks by which a row could hold, tick or subscribe to its own elapsed value: `useState`, `useReducer`, `useSyncExternalStore`, `useEffect` and `useLayoutEffect`, each matched as a whole identifier. This follows the suite's criterion 'no timer and no clock' (file docblock lines 4-10). Evidence: a must-match fixture table in that file, one source fixture per barred hook (5 fixtures), with each predicted and asserted to match. Run by `npm test -- src/renderer/src/lanes/LaneRow.source.test.ts`.

C9-allows. The same predicate does not flag the hooks a timer-free row may legitimately use. Near-miss fixtures `const ref = useRef<HTMLButtonElement>(null);`, a `useMemo(...)` call and a `useId()` call are each predicted and asserted not to match. This fails at base, where the inline regex `/useState|useEffect|useRef/` (base line 45) matches the `useRef` fixture. Evidence: the same command.

C9-real (deliberately preserved behaviour). The predicate applied to the real `LaneRow.tsx` source finds 0 matches, the predicted count. At base `grep -nE "\buse[A-Z]\w*" src/renderer/src/lanes/LaneRow.tsx` prints nothing, and React's only import there is `memo`. The fixture tests and the real-source test call the same predicate, not a copy of it. Evidence: the same command.

U1-quoted. The retired-id offender scan in `hygiene.test.ts` ('finds no reference to a retired test id outside the one ratified proof'; base line 1360 is `if (text.includes(literal))`) matches a retired literal only as a whole quote-delimited string, single, double or backtick. That is the shape `retiredLiteralUseReport` builds at base line 1195. The scan goes through one named predicate, and the real-tree loop and the fixtures below both call it. Evidence: `npm test -- src/renderer/src/__tests__/hygiene.test.ts` passes.

U1-must-match. Fixtures in `hygiene.test.ts`: code carrying the retired id quoted with `'`, with `"` and with a backtick is each flagged as 1 offence, as predicted and asserted. Needles are assembled from fragments, so the file is not its own violation. Evidence: the same command. Discrimination: break the predicate's quote alternation, observe the failure, revert.

U1-near-miss. A fixture carrying a live id that extends the retired one (assembled as the retired id + `'-x'`, inside quotes) is flagged as 0 offences, as predicted and asserted. This fails at base, where `text.includes` flags it. Evidence: the same command.

U1-real (deliberately preserved behaviour). The real-tree scan still walks more than 100 files and reports `[]` offenders. The predicted count of 0 was measured at base two ways: `git grep -n "'lane-row-pin'" -- src` (quote-delimited; the only occurrence is single-quoted) and `git grep -n lane-row-pin -- src` (substring) each return the single line `src/renderer/src/lanes/LaneRail.test.tsx:180`, which is the exempt file. Evidence: the same command.

U2-two-term. In `PodBar.styles.test.ts`, `borderWidthOffenders('.a { border-width: var(--oc-border-hairline) 0; }')` returns `[]`. It returns 1 offender at base, because `borderWidthIsTokenised` (base lines 448-452) requires a longhand's whole value to be one token. This matches the `PodBar.module.css:2-4` docblock ('Every border width here is `--oc-border-hairline`, `--oc-border-thick` or a bare `0` reset'). Evidence: `npm test -- src/renderer/src/pods/PodBar.styles.test.ts` passes.
U2-four-term. `borderWidthOffenders('.a { border-width: 0 var(--oc-border-thick) 0 var(--oc-border-hairline); }')` returns `[]`. Evidence: the same command.
U2-raw-length. A multi-value `border-width` with a raw length term (`var(--oc-border-hairline) ` + `'1' + 'px'`) returns 1 offender. Evidence: the same command.
U2-wrong-family. A multi-value `border-width` with a wrong-family token (`var(--oc-space-1) 0`) returns 1 offender. Evidence: the same command.
U2-too-many. A `border-width` with five terms (`0 0 0 0 0`) returns 1 offender, because `border-width` takes 1-4 values. Evidence: the same command.
U2-per-side. A per-side longhand with two terms (`border-top-width: var(--oc-border-hairline) 0`) returns 1 offender, because per-side longhands stay single-valued. Evidence: the same command.

U2-axis. The logical axis longhands `border-block-width` and `border-inline-width` accept 1-2 terms, each a width token or `0`. A two-term `border-inline-width: var(--oc-border-hairline) 0` returns `[]`, and a three-term one returns 1 offender. Evidence: the same command.

U2-doc-and-real (deliberately preserved behaviour). The predicate's docblock (base lines 442-447) states the multi-value rule. The existing fixtures at base :462-472 still pass unchanged, and `borderWidthOffenders(css)` over the real `PodBar.module.css` is still `[]`. Evidence: the same command.

T6-scope. The three owned files pass together: `npm test -- src/renderer/src/lanes/LaneRow.source.test.ts src/renderer/src/__tests__/hygiene.test.ts src/renderer/src/pods/PodBar.styles.test.ts` exits 0. Every injection T6 makes is into a predicate in a file it owns, not into production code.
